title: Synthetic Socratic Debates: Examining Persona Effects on Moral Decision and Persuasion Dynamics

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing moral judgments, debate consensus rates, and persuasion strategies across AI agents assigned different age personas ranging from 20 to 60.
Evaluating differences in moral blameworthiness scores, moral foundation alignment, and debate outcomes across agents assigned male, female, and non-binary personas.
Analyzing the moral reasoning and persuasion dynamics of agents prompted with different country-of-residence backgrounds (e.g., US, China, Brazil, France, Nigeria, India).
Measuring variations in moral decisions and rhetorical strategies (Ethos, Pathos, Logos) across agents assigned lower, middle, and upper social class personas.
Assessing differences in moral judgments and multi-turn debate success across agents prompted with different political ideologies (e.g., libertarian-left vs. authoritarian-right).
Measuring the impact of assigned Big Five personality traits on agents' moral reasoning, persuasion effectiveness, and rhetorical styles during structured debates.
